lead.kicker: TOP STORY  •  YEMEN AND SAUDI ARABIA
lead.headline: Riyadh's Airport Stays Shut as the US Weighs Joining Yemen's War
lead.deck: Saudi Arabia reports a new barrage of drones and missiles.
body: Picture a fight inside one house that has now crossed into the neighbour's yard. Yemen's internationally recognised government is fighting the Houthis, a movement backed by Iran, and Saudi Arabia, Yemen's neighbour, backs the government with an air campaign. Saudi Arabia has reportedly carried out hundreds of strikes on Houthi-held areas, including the capital Sanaa. The Houthis answered by declaring Saudi airspace a zone of military operations and have now struck Saudi Arabia itself.

On Saturday 10 October they hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said at least 12 people were killed and at least 309 wounded. The dead included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt. It was the third Houthi attack on that airport in a week, and the Saudi-led coalition called it a war crime.

The attacks continue. Saudi Arabia reported a new barrage of drones and missiles on 12 October, and Riyadh airport remains shut. President Trump says he is considering joining the Saudi-led offensive, which aims to push the Houthis from Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. A Houthi leader warned the US would face a swift and painful response. The UN says more than 217,000 people have been displaced since fighting escalated on Yemen's west coast.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent attacks days before the weekend strikes and has not explained why. Yemen's Saudi-backed government says Houthi strikes over 24 hours killed at least five civilians, including in an attack on a hospital in Taiz. Iran says it is ready to help facilitate dialogue between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia.

world.headline: Drones Hit Two Ships Off Bulgaria as Trump's Energy Pause Is Denied
world.deck: Eleven sailors are missing after one ship sank in the Black Sea.
body: Bulgaria sits on the western shore of the Black Sea. Its Prime Minister, Rumen Radev, says drones struck two ships off its coast, and one sank. Rescuers evacuated 15 crew (seven Ukrainian, eight Azerbaijani) and rescued one sailor from the sunken ship, but 11 sailors are missing.

Bulgaria summoned Russia's ambassador without formally accusing Russia. Mr Radev said there is no solid evidence against a specific party, but that the outcome favours Russia. Bulgaria is a member of the EU and of NATO, an alliance of countries that protect each other. Ukraine and Russia, which are at war, both have shores on the Black Sea.

Meanwhile, on Sunday 11 October President Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire, a promise to stop hitting each other's energy sites. By Monday both sides had denied it. Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said Ukraine had held back from attacking Russian energy sites, while Russia kept attacking Ukraine's. A Russian strike on a high-rise in a Kyiv suburb killed at least two people on Monday evening.

US envoys told Ukrainian officials that a deal allowing Russian diesel exports is meant to draw Russia back to talks, though they said Mr Putin was not ready to negotiate an end to the war. Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi, the former head of Ukraine's forces, told the BBC that Ukraine has stabilised the front line and broken Russia's ability to advance.

Warnings came from elsewhere in Europe too. Czech intelligence chief Michal Koudelka said Russia could pursue riskier operations in NATO states that support Ukraine within months. NATO's top commander, Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, told a forum in Warsaw that the alliance would be ready to fight tonight if attacked.

india.headline: Youth Leaders Detained as India's Voter-List Fight Goes to Court
india.deck: Protesters want the chief election commissioner to resign.
body: A voter list is the official list of people allowed to vote. India's Election Commission has been revising it through the Special Intensive Revision. Critics say it has led to the deletion of more than 130 million people from voter lists since 2025. The Commission and the government reject the allegations, saying the exercise has no political motive and aims to remove duplicate and ineligible entries.

On 5 October a three-judge Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notices to the government, the Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The court said that if it finds the law was not followed, it can undo the revision.

On Monday, leaders of the Cockroach youth movement were detained after entering Jantar Mantar, a protest site in Delhi, demanding that Mr Kumar resign. Delhi Police said Jantar Mantar is no longer an official protest site. Before a bigger protest on 10 October, tens of thousands of police were deployed in Delhi and the Metro closed 57 stations.
india.why: Voter lists decide who can vote, so disputes over them test how courts protect the right to vote.
also: Courts: the Supreme Court told the Centre that restrictions on protests must be proportionate and urged it to name another protest venue.
Protests: Cockroach leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released after about 24 hours.

us.headline: Six Senators Say Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Should Be Reversed
us.deck: Four Republicans and two Democrats object. Diesel was $6.23 a gallon on Friday.
body: Diesel powers trucks, trains and farm machines, so its price affects what goods cost. According to AAA, the US national average was $6.23 a gallon on Friday, after hitting a record $6.52 on 22 September.

Last week President Trump announced a deal with Russia's President Putin: Russia would supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, then 500,000 tons in November, 1 million tons after that, and 3 million tons more within a short period. The Treasury issued a temporary licence allowing the sales.

Six senators, four Republicans and two Democrats, say the White House did not consult Congress as a statute requires, and that the plan runs against the 2022 law banning Russian energy imports. On Monday Mr Trump defended a Treasury waiver allowing Russian fuel imports through April and said he made the right choice. An energy expert quoted by AP said the deal is unlikely to make a dent in pump prices.

us.why: Fuel prices touch almost every price in a shop, and this fight shows how Congress limits a president.
us.analyst: Does a deal for 300,000 tons change a national price much? Why might senators of both parties object to a plan meant to lower prices?
